newsitem.title: USA: Two more Georgia counties plan school tax votes.
newsitem.headline: Two more Georgia counties plan school tax votes.

text.p: Two more Georgia counties, Columbia and Jackson, have approved March 18 referendums on the state's newly authorized sales tax increase for school contruction.

The proposal would raise $40 million in Columbia County, which would use $27.6 million to pay off existing debt and $11.2 million for new construction. If approved, the county would reduce its property tax rate for schools by 1.25 mills.
In Jackson County, the tax would raise $25 million. The county school district would get almost $17 million, using $9 million to retire oustanding bond debt and $8 million for construction.
City of Jefferson's school district would get $4.2 million, using $1 million to pay off bond debt and $3.2 million to add classrooms.
The remaining $3.9 million would go to Commerce City School District, which would use the entire amount for construction and renovation.

A dozen counties have approved March referendums since November, when Georgia voters approved a constitutional amendment allowing school districts to seek one-cent sales tax hikes for five years to build new schools or retire construction debt. Previously, only property taxes could be used or school contruction.
